approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted molecules using connected-fragment crossover, ordinary mutation walks, canonical identity checks and a source-relative sulfur gate. It retains the full accepted archive and breeds from sixty-four high-scoring survivors. Before each batch it fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process and a fixed XGBoost pair regressor to real labels from the current session. The pair model predicts raw score differences; averaging each accepted reference label plus its directed difference gives each candidate its active predictive location. The original GP still supplies correlated residual draws and, after three non-improving batches, eligibility for the forty highest GP means. Successive available sampled maxima buy the batch, and actual feedback updates both models, the archive, survivors and later breeding.
approach.novelty: This single contribution test removes cross-candidate residual dependence at every successful allocation. Each candidate keeps its all-reference predictive location and actual jittered marginal residual variance; the existing independent normal coordinate is multiplied by the full norm of its original Cholesky row. The original correlated all-reference law remains a passive same-state comparison. There are no completed same-Parent siblings in the brief. The concurrent tickets change reciprocity, scalar prediction structure or learned predictor weights; this ticket changes none of those. Earlier correlation removals used a restricted Gaussian consumer, a winner-probability consumer or native quantile marginals. The new evidence concerns correlation only within this all-reference cardinal composition, with a working prediction that removing useful retained dependence will reduce the complete endpoint mean.

On those actual purchases, all-reference MSE 0.008649387924947863 improves on incumbent-reference 0.00918329073879438 but remains worse than the same-state GP 0.0054658416803000385. These quantities were independently traced to the original logs and trajectories of every issued Search cell in policy/scratch/r0073-03-improve-L01/parent-evidence-audit.json and its 15 audit-seed files; the displayed endpoint figures retain the frozen protocol aggregate rounding. This motivates an unanswered component question, not a claim that correlation is harmful. The scoped positive restricted-only Gaussian removal n-5e03d3ccd1b7 and all-allocation qPO removal n-61819156f98f use different locations, objectives and exposure conditions; neither answers this cardinal-consumer question. literature_review.conclusion: Carry the exact frozen w8-cardinal-structure-and-consumer-review source records and recorded queries; they were executed by Search Policy, not rerun by this PLAN. The review assigns reciprocal inference, scalar-potential fitting and chronological stacking to other portfolio positions and defers neural cycle-loss training. None of those elements is adopted here, and there is no paper-setting deviation to claim for an unadopted method. Their original applicability text is retained verbatim as provenance, not relabeled as this slot. The all-reference predictor, its inherited PADRE adaptation, fixed XGBoost model and GP source are preserved code-Parent capabilities, not newly introduced assets or model uses. The exact conditional covariance calculation and authorized Search evidence supply this one dependence intervention. No primary-paper score, asymptotic guarantee, source code, pretrained checkpoint, dataset, extra model or package transfers. The direct predictive counterexamples, incomplete native control, formal-Anchor criterion mismatch and unknown whole-job GPU peak remain explicit.

Its changed all-reference location leaves retained dependence unpriced; earlier isolated Gaussian/qPO tests motivate the working directional prediction only under their original scopes, and the incomplete native result supplies no signed contribution. No literature-derived predictor operation is introduced in this control, so its adoption list is intentionally empty.

hypothesis: On every successful allocation of the unchanged raw all-reference Parent, replace only cross-candidate GP residual dependence: for original normal tensor Z, successful jittered factor L and raw scale s, use R_ind[r,i]=s*Z[r,i]*sqrt(sum_j L[i,j]^2) instead of s*(Z@L.T)[r,i]. Preserve active all-reference location, actual marginal variances, nonzero residuals, original-GP-mean mask, all normal calls and sequential selection. Write a_i for the unchanged raw all-reference location, d_i=sqrt(sum_j L_ij^2), and s for the unchanged raw score scale. The active law is A_ind[r,i]=a_i+s*Z[r,i]*d_i; the passive original law is A_corr[r,i]=a_i+s*(Z@L.T)[r,i]. Conditional on each current accepted state, both laws have mean a_i and variance s^2*d_i^2; the independent law has exactly zero analytic off-diagonal residual covariance before sequential selection. This does not set empirical draw means or covariances, make selected identities independent, or remove nonzero residual influence. The predicted activation is changed actual paid identities after these preservation checks. A complete signed matched endpoint contrast then prices retained dependence only in this composition.

finding_summary.headline: Removing residual dependence changed purchases and lowered the endpoint mean by 0.01314
finding_summary.insights:
This settles an exposed, marginal-preserving contribution test for correlation under the all-reference cardinal location. It rules out dormancy, lost residual variance, altered random consumption or missing feedback as explanations of this contrast. It does not establish a uniform task benefit, a reliable population effect, contribution in other consumers, or a chemical cause for the loss. Earlier positive restricted-Gaussian and qPO controls keep their different scopes; the incomplete native-marginal control remains unresolved. The continuation tests a different consumer component using capabilities already present in its Parent. Its literature adoption list is intentionally empty: the inherited pair model was retained, and none of the other portfolio's borrowed predictor operations was introduced.

The remaining ranking limitation is visible on the realized stream. All-reference paid MSE was 0.010786 versus 0.006499 for the GP, worse in all 15 cells; tie-half ordering accuracy was 63.24% versus 67.92%. The corresponding Parent MSE was 0.008649, but that cross-run change follows different purchases, not changed same-state means. Late incumbent-gain mass fell from 1.753579 to 1.060070 even though full positive gains over generating parents rose from 14.330552 to 14.819591. More small parent-relative progress therefore does not establish better endpoints; incumbent mass itself telescopes to endpoint progress and supplies no independent mediation evidence.

Chemistry adds a proposal limitation, not a causal explanation. Generic scaffold count rose from 1,240 to 1,423 and fragment-excluded within-batch similarity fell from 0.749127 to 0.736552, yet related aromatic/carbonyl and amine families, extended assemblies and unusual bond environments persisted. The admitted report records 1,185 N-halogen-bearing purchases versus 760 and no explicit charge or assigned stereochemical alternatives. This is not universal scaffold collapse, nor evidence that broader topology is better chemistry. A different ranking model could address the measured prediction gap; chemically coherent core/linker proposals or a search scheme preserving distinct functional-group families could address the observed local alternatives. Their endpoint benefit, the wider approach, formal-Anchor gaps and whole-job GPU peaks remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The intended dependence removal operated in all 435 allocations. All-reference locations and actual jittered marginal variances were preserved, all 69,600 candidate marginal variances remained positive, and the independent law had zero analytic cross-candidate residual covariance. Reconstruction errors stayed below 1e-15. It changed 411 purchased sets and 1,148 accepted identities relative to the correlated law on the same states; 13 additional batches changed order only. Every one of the 15 sessions was exposed. All 4,350 purchases joined to actual feedback, 4,200 entered both next fits, and 150 final-batch purchases were explicitly censored.

The complete endpoint mean fell from 0.547030 to 0.533892: Child minus code Parent was -0.013138. This exceeds the registered 0.002 descriptive removal-loss scale and supports positive retained-correlation contribution in this composition. The expected decrease was observed and no registered falsifier triggered. The result is uneven: seed macro changes were +0.019595, +0.002693 and -0.061702; seven endpoint cells improved and eight declined. The largest loss was -0.210799 in the third sitagliptin session, alongside a +0.171430 gain in its first session. Mean docking and zaleplon endpoints fell by 0.049459 and 0.027004. The separate +0.002 developmental gain target failed; the literal formal-Anchor criterion remains inapplicable because this Child has a different code Parent.

molecular.headline: Aromatic rings, cyclic amines and carbonyl heterocycles, with broader scaffolds but frequent N-halogen bonds and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All 15 original Child and 15 published code-Parent Search trajectories were read in evaluation order for frozen seeds 0/1/2, with 300 accepted records in every cell. Each node contributes 4,350 accepted optimizer purchases and 150 initial observations. The descriptors below exclude initials unless stated; these are scored purchases, not every unpurchased graph the generator considered. The issued digest is reproduced exactly. No trajectory is missing and no covered task is omitted. context.comparison reports both child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, no profile-mismatched seeds, and the code Parent n-ff10f4d5e7f3. This complete pairing is distinct from merely completing Child evaluation. The output includes substituted aromatic carboxamides and imines, very large aza-aryl/carbonyl assemblies, aryl-substituted cyclic amines, biphenyl-linked cyclic diamides, and fluorinated condensed or bridged carbonyl heterocycles. Digest ring-closure rates are 0.9966–1.0 and aromatic-presence rates 0.9931–1.0. These are string counters, not ring perception or aromatic atom fractions. RDKit finds 4,337 aromatic-containing Child purchases, six acyclic graphs and a median of five perceived rings. Recognizable functional groups coexist with unusual heteroatom–halogen bonds and complex unsaturated ring junctions; the synthetic-plausibility and drug-likeness chips are qualitative structural readings, not route, stability, toxicity, ADME or biological-utility measurements. Child heavy-atom median/range are 31 and 2–118, versus Parent 33 and 1–120. Retaining the historical descriptor boundaries, Child counts at <=5, <=6, >=50 and >50 atoms are 6, 6, 594 and 578; Parent counts are 8, 8, 607 and 597. Of the 594 large Child graphs, 477 occur in one covered objective. Child typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 2,247/1,423 versus Parent 1,969/1,240, including the empty acyclic scaffold. Thus output is not globally collapsed, but pooled scaffold counts do not establish independent chemotypes or better chemistry. Radius-2 chirality-aware 2,048-count Morgan dot-product Tanimoto, using unordered pairs only within each task/seed session, averages 0.639456 for Child versus 0.652628 for Parent; excluding <=6-heavy-atom fragments gives 0.641132 versus 0.654981. Within actual ten-purchase batches the corresponding values are 0.734690 versus 0.746456, or 0.736552 versus 0.749127 after fragment exclusion. These are pair-count-weighted descriptive similarities; there are no cross-session pairs. Child N-halogen, O-halogen and O–O bond counts by molecule are 1,185, 131 and 95 versus Parent 760, 125 and 59. All 4,350 purchases lack formal charges, assigned tetrahedral configurations and specified double-bond geometry; RDKit nevertheless identifies 4,507 unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,503 molecules, versus 6,666 in 2,672 Parent molecules. Neutral depiction does not measure solution protonation, and an unassigned graph does not specify a realizable stereoisomer. The inherited generic [*]=[*]=[*] pattern also matches sulfonyl sulfur. The separate bond-context audit identifies carbon-centred matches in 42 Child versus 276 Parent molecules, and sulfur-centred matches in 218 versus 341; ordinary sulfonyl matches are not treated as cumulene liabilities. Child output includes 31 molecules with a perceived cycle of at most four atoms whose atoms all carry aromatic flags, and 331 molecules with a perceived ring of at least nine atoms, versus Parent 294 and 373. Aromatic atom flags alone do not prove aromaticity of every perceived cycle or geometric feasibility. Top-87 and bottom-87 subsets use the supplied scores among 870 purchases per task with fixed seed/evaluation ties; top/bottom-29 subsets are also retained for each session. These subsets can concentrate in one seed and are not independent replications. Every initial, optimizer, leading, low-scoring and final row remains in the matched cell audits. There is no mechanism-activation, conditional-correlation contribution, selection, statistical-equivalence or chemical-utility conclusion here. liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 287 purchases and 65 of the top-87 subset. They coexist with recognizable amide and ring-nitrogen environments, so graph acceptance does not establish ordinary medicinal-chemistry substitution or synthetic accessibility.
Twenty-five purchases contain an O–O bond. Large linked aromatic combinations at the low-score end add connectivity without showing a usable synthetic route or a beneficial observed gradient.

Compact alternative cores are present, but no explicit stereochemical or charge-state alternatives accompany the new partially saturated ring and imine connectivity. Their value cannot be inferred from the depicted neutral graphs.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
